mainTopic: The שולחן and the coated מזבחות and whether they can become טמא, a person's table as a source of כפרה, and protection from the fire of גיהנם, closing מסכת חגיגה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier proof. The gold-coated שולחן still counts as a wooden item, because the פסוק in יחזקאל calls it 'wood'. The גמרא notices that this פסוק starts with 'מזבח' and ends with 'שולחן'. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש explain that today a person's table atones for him the way the מזבח once did. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה, where רבי אליעזר says the two מזבחות are like the ground and cannot become טמא, and it brings פסוקים for both the copper and the golden מזבח. The חכמים's reason, 'because they are coated', looks backwards, so the גמרא gives two answers. In the first, the חכמים say the coating makes the מזבחות able to become טמא. In the second, they agree the מזבחות are pure, but say the coating is nullified, so 'like the ground' is not needed. The amud ends with two קל וחומר teachings: the fire of גיהנם cannot harm תלמידי חכמים, and it cannot harm even the sinners of ישראל, who are full of מצוות like a pomegranate. Then the הדרן closes פרק חומר בקודש and all of מסכת חגיגה.

steps.title: The table is called 'wood' in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier point. The שולחן keeps the status of a wooden vessel even though it is coated, because the פסוק in יחזקאל calls it 'wood'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the Torah calls it 'wood', as it says: 'The altar, of wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits, its corners, its length and its walls of wood. And he said to me: This is the table that is before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a thought from the previous page. It brings a פסוק showing that the שולחן counts as a wooden item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain wooden item that is not moved around normally would not become טמא. So if the שולחן still counts as 'wood' despite its gold coating, there must be another reason it can become טמא: it was taken out and shown to the people who came for the רגל. The פסוק is the source that the שולחן is still called 'wood'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
Wood
The table in the בית המקדש that held the לחם הפנים
As it is written

phrases.english: because the Merciful One called it "wood,"
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page about why the שולחן is treated as a wooden item.

steps.raayaObject: That the gold-coated שולחן still counts as a wooden item

steps.title: The verse starts with 'altar' and ends with 'table'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out something strange in the פסוק it just quoted. It calls the item a מזבח at the start and a שולחן at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק began with 'altar' and ended with 'table'!
steps.whatsHappening: Having quoted the פסוק, the גמרא notices that it calls the same item by two different names. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק should not switch names for no reason. Calling one item both a מזבח and a שולחן suggests there is a lesson hidden in the switch.

keyTerms.meaning: It opened or began with
It finished or ended with
Altar

phrases.english: It opened with "altar"
and ended with "table"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the wording of the פסוק quoted in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses two different names for one item, so something must explain the switch

steps.title: Today a person's table atones like the altar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש explain the switch. While the בית המקדש stood, the מזבח brought כפרה. Now a person's own table brings him כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say: When the בית המקדש stands, the מזבח atones for a person. Now, a person's table atones for him.
steps.whatsHappening: Two great אמוראים explain why the פסוק calls a table a מזבח. A person's table takes the place of the מזבח today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The switch from 'מזבח' to 'שולחן' teaches that after the בית המקדש, a person's table does the job the מזבח did, and brings כפרה. The table atones when he uses it well, for example by feeding guests and poor people.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Standing, still existing
Atones, brings כפרה
Now

steps.whatToRemember: Without a בית המקדש, a person's table, used for kindness to others, takes the place of the מזבח in bringing כפרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous teaching about how a Jewish home and its table can carry holiness even without a בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish
who both say:
When the Temple is standing,
the altar atones for a person;
now, a person's table
atones for him.
phrases.notes: He means a table where guests and poor people are fed.

steps.title: The copper altar is like the ground
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, where רבי אליעזר says the two מזבחות do not need טבילה because they are like the ground. For the copper מזבח, the source is the פסוק calling it a 'מזבח of earth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: All the vessels in the בית המקדש had second sets, and so on. The copper מזבח is like the ground, as it says: 'An altar of earth you shall make for Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and starts giving the sources for its rule. First it shows that the copper מזבח counts as ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things attached to the ground, or counted as ground, cannot become טמא. The Torah calls the outer מזבח a 'מזבח אדמה', an altar of earth, so even though it has a copper covering it counts as ground.

keyTerms.meaning: Second ones, meaning backup sets of vessels
The copper (outer) altar
An altar of earth

phrases.english: All the vessels that were in the Temple
had second ones, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה: all the vessels needed טבילה except the two מזבחות, which are like the ground.

phrases.english: The copper altar:
as it is written: "An altar of earth
you shall make for Me."

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שְׁנִיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the side teaching
steps.raayaObject: That the copper מזבח is like the ground and cannot become טמא

steps.title: The golden altar is compared to the copper altar
steps.stepSummary: For the golden מזבח, the גמרא uses a פסוק that says 'the altars' in plural. That links the two מזבחות together, so the golden one is also like the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: The golden מזבח: as it says, 'The menorah and the altars.' The two altars are compared to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the second מזבח. One word in the plural ties the two altars together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No פסוק calls the golden מזבח 'earth'. But the word 'מזבחות' puts both altars in one phrase, which is a היקש, a comparison. So whatever is true of the copper מזבח, being like the ground, is also true of the golden one.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden (inner) altar
They are compared, through a היקש
A comparison between two things placed together in a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The copper מזבח is 'earth' straight from the פסוק, and the golden מזבח gets the same status through a היקש with it.

phrases.english: The golden altar:
as it is written: "The menorah and the altars"
the altars are compared to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'like the ground' status from the copper מזבח to the golden one
steps.raayaObject: That the golden מזבח is also like the ground
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 3:31, 'והמזבחות', which makes a היקש between the two altars

steps.title: Being coated should make the altars impure, not pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה, who seem to say the מזבחות stay pure because they are coated. It challenges this: a metal coating is exactly what should let them become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: Because they are coated. On the contrary! Since they are coated, they should become טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first quotes the חכמים's line from the משנה as a setup. Then it attacks that line, because the reason seems to point the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the משנה has the חכמים giving a different reason why the מזבחות stay pure: their coating. But a metal coating makes the whole item count as a metal vessel, and metal vessels can become טמא. So the coating should be a reason for טומאה, not against it.

keyTerms.meaning: Coated, covered with metal plating
On the contrary
They become טמא
They are

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'because they are coated' as a reason the מזבחות stay pure. A metal coating normally points toward טומאה. Steps 7 and 8 give two different ways to understand the חכמים.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Because they are coated.
On the contrary:
since they are coated,
they should become impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְצוּפִּין אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי אליעזר's reason to the חכמים's line in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's statement in the משנה, 'because they are coated'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A metal coating makes an item count as metal, which can become טמא, so the coating cannot be a reason for purity

steps.title: Reread the משנה: the חכמים say the altars can become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה. The חכמים do not give another reason for purity. They disagree completely and say the מזבחות can become טמא because of their metal coating.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say it this way: And the חכמים declare them able to become טמא, because they are coated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the משנה so the חכמים's reason makes sense. They hold that the מזבחות can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one added word, 'מטמאין', the coating becomes a reason for טומאה, which fits how metal works. Now there is a real מחלוקת: רבי אליעזר says the מזבחות are pure because they are like the ground, and the חכמים say they can become טמא because they are coated with metal.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, meaning read the text this way
They declare it able to become טמא

steps.whatToRemember: In this first answer, רבי אליעזר says the מזבחות are pure because they are like the ground, and the חכמים say they can become טמא because they are coated with metal. The next step gives a second answer.

phrases.english: Say: And the Rabbis declare them susceptible to impurity,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adding the word 'מטמאין' to the משנה, so the חכמים fully disagree with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: because they are coated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by rereading the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים seemed to give 'coated' as a reason for purity
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים say the מזבחות can become טמא because their metal coating makes them metal vessels

steps.title: A second answer: the coating does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another answer. It keeps the wording of the משנה. The חכמים are asking רבי אליעזר why he needed the reason 'like the ground.' Was he worried about the metal coating? That coating is nullified to the wood anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you like, say this: the חכמים were speaking to רבי אליעזר. 'What is your thinking? Did you say they are like the ground because they are coated with metal? Their coating is completely nullified to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to answer the question from Step 6. This time it does not change the meaning of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the חכמים disagreed with רבי אליעזר and said the מזבחות can become טמא. Here they agree the מזבחות stay pure, but they reject his reason. For these מזבחות the coating is nullified to the wood, so they count as wood and not metal. That means there was no need to say they are 'like the ground.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say': this opens a second, alternative answer
What is your reasoning?
Coated (with metal)
It is completely nullified; it does not count on its own

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this answer up with Step 7. In Step 7 the חכמים say the מזבחות CAN become טמא. In this answer the חכמים agree they stay pure. They only disagree with רבי אליעזר's reason.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. In the first, the חכמים argue on the הלכה: the coating makes the מזבחות טמא. In the second, they argue only on the reason: the coating is nullified, so there is no need for 'like the ground.'

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
The Rabbis were saying to Rabbi Eliezer:
What is your reasoning?
Is it because they are coated?
Their coating is completely nullified to them.

steps.title: The fire of גיהנם cannot touch תלמידי חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי אלעזר: the fire of גיהנם has no power over תלמידי חכמים. He proves it with a קל וחומר from the salamander.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי אלעזר: the fire of גיהנם has no power over תלמידי חכמים. We learn it with a קל וחומר from the salamander. The salamander is only something that comes from fire. Yet if a person rubs himself with its blood, fire has no power over him. תלמידי חכמים have bodies that are completely fire, as it says 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳.' So fire surely has no power over them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from הלכה to אגדה. It brings a teaching that the fire of גיהנם cannot harm תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a קל וחומר, which means 'if the small case is true, the big case is surely true.' The salamander is only a product of fire, yet its blood protects against fire. תלמידי חכמים are filled with תורה, which the פסוק calls fire, so they are protected even more.

keyTerms.meaning: Torah scholars
The place of punishment after death
A logical proof: if it is true in the lesser case, it is surely true in the greater case
Salamander, a creature believed to come out of fire
All the more so (the closing words of a קל וחומר)

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא moves straight from the coated מזבח into this אגדה about fire. It sets up the next teaching, which uses the מזבח itself as its proof.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:

phrases.english: The fire of Gehinnom has no power over Torah scholars,
by a kal vachomer from the salamander:
If a salamander, which is just a product of fire —

phrases.aramaic: הַסָּךְ מִדָּמָהּ אֵין אוּר שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: whoever smears himself with its blood, fire has no power over him,
then Torah scholars, whose whole body is fire,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״הֲלוֹא כֹה דְבָרִי כָּאֵשׁ נְאֻם ה׳״ —
phrases.english: as it is written: 'Is not My word like fire, says ה׳' —
all the more so!

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fire of גיהנם has no power over תלמידי חכמים, learned by a קל וחומר from the salamander

steps.title: Even the sinners of ישראל are protected from גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the fire of גיהנם has no power even over the sinners of ישראל. He learns it by a קל וחומר from the מזבח הזהב. Its thin gold coating was never burned through, and even the 'empty' Jews are full of מצוות like a pomegranate.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: the fire of גיהנם has no power over the sinners of ישראל. We learn it with a קל וחומר from the golden מזבח. That מזבח had gold only as thick as a gold coin, yet for many years the fire had no power over it. The sinners of ישראל are full of מצוות like a pomegranate, as it says 'like a split pomegranate is your רקה.' Do not read it 'רקתך.' Read it 'רקנין שבך,' the empty ones among you. So fire surely has no power over them.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש goes even further than רבי אלעזר. The fire of גיהנם cannot harm even the sinners of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small side is the golden מזבח. It had only a coin-thin layer of gold, yet the fire burning on it for years never destroyed it. The big side is the sinners of ישראל, who are full of מצוות. A דרשה reads 'רקתך' as 'רקנין,' the empty people, to show that even they are full of מצוות like a pomegranate is full of seeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The sinners of the Jewish people
The golden מזבח, where the קטורת was burned
A gold coin, used here to show how thin the coating was
'Do not read': a דרשה that reads a word in a different way
Empty ones, people who seem to have no good deeds

steps.whatToRemember: There are two קל וחומר teachings. רבי אלעזר says תלמידי חכמים are protected, like the salamander. ריש לקיש says even the sinners of ישראל are protected, like the thin gold of the מזבח הזהב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the אגדה back to the topic of the סוגיא. The coating of the golden מזבח, which mattered for the laws of טומאה, becomes the source for a lesson about the hidden good in every Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אֵין אוּר שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם שׁוֹלֶטֶת בְּפוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: The fire of Gehinnom has no power over the sinners of Israel,
by a kal vachomer from the golden altar:
If the golden altar,

phrases.english: which has on it only the thickness of a gold dinar —

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה שָׁנִים אֵין הָאוּר שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: for many years the fire had no power over it,
then the sinners of Israel, who are full of מצוות like a pomegranate,
as it is written: 'Like a split pomegranate is your temple,'
do not read 'rakatekh' but 'the empty ones among you' —
all the more so!

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fire of גיהנם has no power over the sinners of ישראל, learned by a קל וחומר from the מזבח הזהב, because even the 'empty' Jews are full of מצוות

steps.title: הדרן: Closing פרק חומר בקודש and finishing מסכת חגיגה
steps.stepSummary: The traditional הדרן formula closes פרק חומר בקודש and announces that מסכת חגיגה is finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק חומר בקודש, and מסכת חגיגה is now complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line that says goodbye to the last פרק and marks the end of מסכת חגיגה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן עלך means 'we will return to you.' It is a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. Because חומר בקודש is the last פרק, the line also says that the whole מסכת is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the standard farewell said at the end of every פרק.
The name of the third and last פרק of חגיגה, taken from its opening words about the stricter rules of קודש.
It is finished, it has come to an end.
The tractate about the duties of ראייה and the חגיגה offering on the שלוש רגלים, and the laws of טומאה and טהרה.

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת חגיגה ends on a hopeful note. Just before this line, ריש לקיש taught that even the 'empty' Jews are full of מצוות and are saved from the fire of גיהנם. The הדרן is a promise to keep coming back to this learning.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Stringency in Holiness"
and Tractate Chagigah is concluded

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ חוֹמֶר בַּקּוֹדֶשׁ וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ מַסֶּכֶת חֲגִיגָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת right after ריש לקיש's teaching about the מזבח הזהב and the sinners of ישראל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק חומר בקודש is finished, and with it מסכת חגיגה is complete, with a promise to return and learn it again.
